rankingModel.rationale: Michelin and James Beard judge food specifically; crowd ratings measure whole-experience satisfaction and are better at detecting badness than greatness. Thin review samples are shrunk toward the prior.
rankingModel.slateRule: Order by food-first score, but compose the five so both kinds of evidence are represented. Expert- and critic-backed picks lead. At least one slot is reserved for the strongest crowd-verified local favorite (highest adjusted rating with a meaningful review base) even when an expert-backed candidate would otherwise take it. A beloved neighborhood spot with no Michelin attention still belongs on the list; it just doesn't lead it.

high_end_dc.name: Albi

reservationDifficulty.label: Very Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Washingtonian's reigning #1 restaurant; Resy tables for the hearth-side seats go within minutes of release.

high_end_dc.why: Michael Rafidi's live-fire Palestinian tasting menu is the most emotionally resonant fine dining in the city — Michelin star, James Beard win, and Washingtonian's top spot two years running.

high_end_dc.name: Omakase at Barracks Row

reservationDifficulty.label: Very Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Small counter, Michelin star and Washingtonian #4 — book 4–6 weeks ahead.

high_end_dc.reservationNote: Book on Resy; Tue–Sat 5:30–11 PM, closed Sun–Mon. Phone (202) 481-1640.
high_end_dc.why: Nakazawa-trained Ricky Wang's counter moves from sweet shrimp in smoked uni sauce to hay-smoked mackerel nigiri with exacting rice and fish — the city's most thrilling omakase at its price.

high_end_dc.name: Jônt

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Single nightly seating at a tiny counter above Maketto; books out weeks ahead.

high_end_dc.why: A blink-and-you'll-miss-it counter earning two Michelin stars for technically dazzling French-meets-Japanese courses in a room that seats barely a dozen.

high_end_dc.name: Fiola

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Prime weekend tables need 2-3 weeks' notice; walk-ins rarely land a seat.

high_end_dc.why: Fabio Trabocchi's marble-and-crystal dining room delivers hand-rolled-pasta grandeur with a nearly thousand-review track record of consistency.

high_end_dc.name: Minibar by José Andrés

reservationDifficulty.label: Very Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Only ~14 seats; reservations release online at an exact time each quarter and vanish within seconds.

high_end_dc.why: José Andrés's original theater-of-the-absurd tasting counter still out-imagines every other kitchen in the city.

high_end_mclean_tysons.name: L'Auberge Chez François

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Reservations release roughly 60 days out; prime weekend slots for the eight-course menu vanish fast.

high_end_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Phone/walk-in only — call ahead, no online booking.
high_end_mclean_tysons.why: A century-old Alsatian institution in a Great Falls farmhouse that still out-romances every newer tasting menu in the region.

high_end_mclean_tysons.name: Ingle Korean Steakhouse

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: NoVA Magazine's #3 restaurant for 2026 and a Washingtonian 100 regular; prime weekend dinner slots go well in advance, though walk-ins are accepted.

high_end_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Not bookable on OpenTable; reserve via inglekoreansteakhouse.com or call (202) 845-4966 (number on its OpenTable listing). Walk-ins accepted.
high_end_mclean_tysons.why: Dry-aged and American Wagyu cuts seared on brass grills set into granite tables, framed by a $79 prix fixe of tartare, cod-roe toast and banchan that turns Korean barbecue into a polished steakhouse ritual.

high_end_mclean_tysons.name: Nostos

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Bookable a few weeks out on OpenTable; Friday/Saturday prime times go first.

high_end_mclean_tysons.why: Tableside saganaki flames and whole grilled fish turn a Tysons office-park address into the DMV's most convincing Athens stand-in.

high_end_mclean_tysons.name: Modan

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: The omakase counter seats only 8–10 at 5:30 and 8:30 and needs a $50 deposit, so book about a week ahead; à la carte tables are easier.

high_end_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Book online (OpenTable). Omakase is $170 or $260 per person with a $50 deposit, forfeited if you cancel within 24 hours.
high_end_mclean_tysons.why: Ex-Nobu chef Chico Dator serves Hokkaido uni and soy-cured bluefin with Tokyo-grade precision, and his miso black cod is juicier and less cloying than the dish it riffs on.

high_end_mclean_tysons.name: Wren

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: OpenTable shows broad same-week availability; weekend prime time fills a few days out.

high_end_mclean_tysons.why: Chef Yo Matsuzaki runs an izakaya with real backbone, from rich ramen to robata-style small plates and an 18–20-course omakase, 14 floors above Tysons.

high_end_nova.name: Nasime

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: ~20 seats, tasting-menu only, dinner Tue–Sat; weekends fill 2–3 weeks out.

high_end_nova.reservationNote: Reserve via nasimerestaurant.com or call (703) 548-1848; book 2–3 weeks ahead for weekends.
high_end_nova.why: Ginza-trained Yuh Shimomura's seven-course menu — pristine sashimi, spiny-lobster cake, soy-maple duck — is quiet, exacting Japanese cooking at a price that feels like a misprint.

high_end_nova.name: Elyse

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Only 30 seats and a single nightly tasting seating; reserve well in advance.

high_end_nova.why: A 30-seat speakeasy tasting counter where a chef at the top of his game turns a strip-mall address into the most intentional five courses in Fairfax.

high_end_nova.name: Clarity

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Tasting-menu seatings are limited nightly; book 2-3 weeks ahead for weekends.

high_end_nova.why: A kitchen that treats a Vienna strip-mall storefront as a stage for genuine special-occasion cooking, plated like still-lifes.

high_end_nova.name: Le Refuge

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Small, snug dining room; call ahead for weekend evenings.

high_end_nova.reservationNote: Phone/walk-in only — call ahead, no online booking.
high_end_nova.why: Unapologetically old-school bouillabaisse-and-duck-a-l'orange cooking that has outlasted every trend in Old Town for three decades.

high_end_nova.name: Harrimans Grill

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: OpenTable advises booking 2–3 weeks ahead; ~20 bookings/day; dinner Wed–Sun only.

high_end_nova.reservationNote: Book on OpenTable 2–3 weeks out for weekend dinner; dinner Wed–Sun 5–9:30 PM.
high_end_nova.why: Hunt-country sourcing meets serious grill technique — wood-fired local beef and Chesapeake seafood plated with resort-level polish, making it the most complete destination dinner in Loudoun.

moderate_dc.name: Daru

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Weekend Resy slots vanish fast on James Beard buzz; weeknights and the bar are easier.

moderate_dc.why: Turns Indian comfort food into a genuinely exciting tasting menu at a price that still lets you order a second round of naan without flinching.

moderate_dc.name: Reveler's Hour

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Small wine-bar footprint means Resy tables disappear almost instantly; expect a wait or an early walk-in.

moderate_dc.why: A tiny, glowing wine bar turning out pasta good enough to anchor a splurge-adjacent date night without the splurge-adjacent bill.

moderate_dc.name: Tapori

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Resy books out on weekends but midweek tables and walk-in bar seats are attainable.

moderate_dc.why: South Asian street food as serious craft — chaat and kathi rolls sharp enough to make you forget you're paying moderate-tier prices.

moderate_dc.name: Anju

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Resy tables open weekly and go quickly for weekend prime time, but bar/counter walk-in seats are usually available.

moderate_dc.why: Soulful, funky-fermented Korean plates and the city's best banchan spread make this the rare date-night spot that never feels like it's trying too hard.

moderate_dc.name: All-Purpose Pizzeria (Shaw)

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Resy recommended for weekend dinner; walk-in seats at the bar or patio often available.

moderate_dc.why: Char-blistered pies, punchy pastas, and a smart natural-wine list make this Shaw stalwart the platonic ideal of a neighborhood Italian date-night spot.

moderate_mclean_tysons.name: Joon

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Fine-dining room; book 1-2 weeks ahead for weekends.

moderate_mclean_tysons.why: Chef Najmieh Batmanglij moves Persian cooking well beyond kebabs — the tahdig-topped qaliyeh mahi alone is worth the trip.

moderate_mclean_tysons.name: Aracosia McLean

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Bookable on OpenTable most nights; weekends fill up so reserve a few days out.

moderate_mclean_tysons.why: A quietly extraordinary Afghan kitchen turning kabuli pulao and mantu into date-night food, at a price that makes fine-dining rivals look silly.

moderate_mclean_tysons.name: Patsy's American

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: A big, high-volume room open until 1–2am; bar seats turn over quickly.

moderate_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Check patsysamerican.com for call-ahead or online waitlist options, or call (703) 552-5100. The bar is walk-in.
moderate_mclean_tysons.why: Great American Restaurants' greatest hits, from baby back ribs to smoked-salmon salad, executed with the group's trademark consistency and served until 1am.

moderate_mclean_tysons.name: Jacques' Brasserie at L'Auberge Chez François

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Same-week tables are usually available on OpenTable; weekend dinner is the tight slot.

moderate_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Book online (OpenTable) or call (703) 759-3800. Closed Mon–Tue.
moderate_mclean_tysons.why: The casual sibling of L'Auberge Chez François, serving hearty French brasserie cooking from the same classically trained kitchen at a fraction of the formality and price.

moderate_mclean_tysons.name: Our Mom Eugenia

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Book a few days ahead for Saturday dinner, which has live Greek music; weekday lunch is easy.

moderate_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Book online (OpenTable) or call (703) 870-7807. Wine Wednesdays: half-price bottles with $30pp in food.
moderate_mclean_tysons.why: Family-recipe Greek cooking with a real home-kitchen touch, from mezze to slow-cooked lamb and grilled fish, in a room that comes alive with live Greek music on Saturdays.

moderate_nova.name: Ellie Bird

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Small room — book ahead, especially weekends.

moderate_nova.why: Precise, wood-fired, ingredient-forward American cooking in a small Falls Church spot regional critics have called Michelin-worthy.

moderate_nova.name: Osteria Marzano

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: ~17 OpenTable bookings/day; weekend dinner fills same-week.

moderate_nova.reservationNote: Book on OpenTable a few days ahead for weekends.
moderate_nova.why: An office-park surprise turning out handmade pastas and blistered brick-oven pies with the generosity and technique of a true neighborhood osteria.

moderate_nova.name: Ambar Clarendon

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate-Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Popular for groups and the unlimited-plates format; book ahead for prime weekend slots.

moderate_nova.chainRationale: Small local Balkan group (three DMV rooms) with Washingtonian and Arlington Magazine recognition — a destination, not a convenience chain.

moderate_nova.name: Evelyn Rose

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Newer arrival with a small dining room; reserve ahead for weekend dinners.

moderate_nova.why: A cozy, ingredient-forward newcomer to Church Street that plays it fresh and unfussy — exactly the low-key-special dinner Vienna needed.

moderate_nova.name: Ruthie's All-Day

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Popular neighborhood spot; weekend dinners benefit from a reservation.

moderate_nova.why: Whole-hog, cornbread-and-sorghum Southern cooking that turned a retro diner room into an Arlington institution.

casual_dc.name: Taqueria Habanero

casual_dc.name: Keren Restaurant

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy

casual_dc.name: Dog Tag Bakery

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: Counter-service cafe, walk-in only.

casual_dc.name: Baked and Wired

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: Counter service, no reservations; grab-and-go even when the line's out the door.

casual_dc.why: Georgetown's best cup of coffee comes with a cupcake that actually earns the hype, at prices that predate the neighborhood's gentrification.

casual_dc.name: El Rinconcito Cafe

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: Casual sit-down, no reservations, easy walk-in most nights.

casual_dc.why: Pupusas griddled to order for a few dollars each — the kind of unglamorous spot that makes 'hidden gem' feel like an understatement.

casual_mclean_tysons.name: Listrani's Italian Gourmet & Pizzeria

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: Casual counter-and-table spot; no reservations needed.

casual_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Walk-in or order ahead; open daily 11 AM.
casual_mclean_tysons.why: Scratch-made lasagna, chicken parm and properly charred Neapolitan pies make it the neighborhood's most dependable casual Italian.

casual_mclean_tysons.name: Zamarod Afghan Cuisine

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: A neighborhood dining room where walk-ins are normally fine; call ahead for weekend groups.

casual_mclean_tysons.why: A decade-plus Great Falls fixture serving fragrant quabili palow, char-grilled lamb and beef-filled mantoo with the generosity of a family table.

casual_mclean_tysons.name: Esaan (Esaan Tumbar / Esaan Thai McLean)

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: A tiny 40-seat room where reservations are recommended for weekend dinner.

casual_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Call to reserve; website is esaanmclean.com. Closed Mondays.
casual_mclean_tysons.why: Laos-inflected Isan cooking with real funk and fire: several styles of somtum, punchy larb and a crisp herb-strewn fried rockfish you won't find on a standard Thai menu.

casual_mclean_tysons.name: Autentico

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: A casual neighborhood spot for walk-ins and takeout.

casual_mclean_tysons.why: Sharp, lime-bright ceviche carretillero and a smoky wok-tossed lomo saltado bring real Lima flavor to a Great Falls strip center.

casual_mclean_tysons.name: Amoo's Restaurant

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Call ahead — no online booking; table held on request.

casual_mclean_tysons.why: The chelo kabob McLean regulars measure every other Persian grill against — simple, classic, and consistently right.

casual_nova.name: Maharani Palace

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Reservations recommended for dinner and weekends; bar seating available for walk-ins.

casual_nova.why: A Herndon storefront with white-tablecloth ambition at strip-mall prices — the tandoor (and nearly 4,000 five-star-leaning reviews) don't lie.

casual_nova.name: Stracci Pizza

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy

casual_nova.why: Victor Albisu's hometown taqueria empire never lost the plot — the grilled-guac-and-chorizo taco still tastes handmade, not franchised. This is the pre-approved chain exception: real critical acclaim, not just convenience.

casual_nova.name: Wooboi Hot Chicken

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: Walk-up counter service; order ahead online to skip the line at peak hours.

casual_nova.why: A strip-mall counter that's been quietly out-punching DC's entire fried-chicken-sandwich boom since 2019.

casual_nova.name: Padaek

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Resy recommended; this cult-favorite fills up on weekends.

casual_nova.why: Padaek treats Lao fish sauce like the star ingredient it's named for, and has earned a genuine local cult following well past its original Falls Church spot.

happy_hour_dc.name: Your Only Friend

happy_hour_dc.name: Pearl Dive Oyster Palace

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate

reservationDifficulty.note: Prime-time dinner and weekend brunch need a reservation, but the bar (happy hour 3-6pm weekdays) takes walk-ins.

happy_hour_dc.why: The 'L'Apéro' zinc-bar hour — wine, Ricard, oysters — is the most convincing Parisian pre-dinner ritual in the city.

happy_hour_mclean_tysons.why: Chef Najmieh Batmanglij moves Persian cooking well beyond kebabs — the tahdig-topped qaliyeh mahi alone is worth the trip.

happy_hour_mclean_tysons.name: Neutral Ground Bar + Kitchen

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Weeknights are easy, but the Sunday jazz brunch fills quickly and needs booking several days ahead.

happy_hour_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Book on Resy. Happy hour seating is bar-only, first come, first served.

happy_hour_mclean_tysons.name: Wren

reservationDifficulty.note: Walk-in pub; only St. Patrick's Day and live-music weekend nights get truly packed.

happy_hour_mclean_tysons.why: A 40-plus-year Great Falls institution with a 150-bottle whiskey shelf, a proper pint of Guinness and honest fish and chips — the after-hike drink everyone in the village ends up having.

happy_hour_mclean_tysons.name: Härth

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: Bar seats are walk-in; OpenTable tables are open same-day most nights.

happy_hour_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Book on OpenTable or walk in to the bar.
happy_hour_mclean_tysons.why: A fireplace-lit lounge with its own rooftop beehives behind the honey cocktails — the most grown-up after-work bar in Tysons, with a regional-farm kitchen that's better than a hotel address suggests.

happy_hour_nova.name: Smyrna

reservationDifficulty.note: Small dining room; bar seats for happy hour are the easier ask.

happy_hour_nova.why: Aegean mezze and a tight, well-chosen wine-and-ouzo list turn a modest Old Town storefront into a genuine happy-hour destination.

happy_hour_nova.name: Carbonara

reservationDifficulty.note: Bar seats often available even when the dining room is full.

happy_hour_nova.why: Tableside cheese-wheel carbonara at the bar is one of the best cheap thrills in Arlington, happy hour or not.

happy_hour_nova.name: Ambar Clarendon

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate-Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Popular for groups and the unlimited-plates format; book ahead for prime weekend slots.

happy_hour_nova.why: An unlimited small-plates Balkan blowout of stroganoff, lamb, and pickled everything that turns a weeknight into an occasion without wrecking the budget.

happy_hour_nova.why: A Ballston newcomer already punching above its weight, with a bar program and small-plates menu built for exactly this occasion.

happy_hour_nova.name: Carlyle
